# snrm2

> Compute the [L2-norm][l2-norm] of a single-precision floating-point vector.

<section class="intro">

The [L2-norm][l2-norm] (or Euclidean norm) is defined as

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:l2_norm" align="center" raw="\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i^2} = \sqrt{x_0^2 + x_1^2 + \ldots + x_{N-1}^2}" alt="L2-norm definition."> -->

```math
\lVert\mathbf{x}\rVert_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i^2} = \sqrt{x_0^2 + x_1^2 + \ldots + x_{N-1}^2}
```

<!-- </equation> -->

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var snrm2 = require( '@stdlib/blas/snrm2' );
```

#### snrm2( x\[, dim] )

Computes the [L2-norm][l2-norm] of a single-precision floating-point vector `x`.

```javascript
var Float32Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float32' );
var array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/array' );

var x = array( new Float32Array( [ 1.0, -2.0, 2.0 ] ) );

var y = snrm2( x );
// returns <ndarray>[ 3.0 ]
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **x**: a non-zero-dimensional [`ndarray`][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] whose underlying data type is `float32`.
-   **dim**: dimension for which to compute the [L2-norm][l2-norm]. Must be a negative integer. Negative indices are resolved relative to the last array dimension, with the last dimension corresponding to `-1`. Default: `-1`.

If provided an input [`ndarray`][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] having more than one dimension, the function performs batched computation, such that the function computes the [L2-norm][l2-norm] for each vector in `x` according to the specified dimension index.

```javascript
var Float32Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float32' );
var array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/array' );

var opts = {
    'shape': [ 2, 3 ]
};
var x = array( new Float32Array( [ 1.0, -2.0, 2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 4.0 ] ), opts );

var y = snrm2( x );
// returns <ndarray>[ 3.0, 5.0 ]
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   The function resolves the dimension index for which to compute the [L2-norm][l2-norm] relative to the last [`ndarray`][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] dimension, with the last dimension corresponding to `-1`.
-   The output [`ndarray`][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] has the same data type as the input [`ndarray`][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] and has a shape which excludes the reduced dimension.
-   If provided an empty vector, the [L2-norm][l2-norm] is `0`.
-   `snrm2()` provides a higher-level interface to the [BLAS][blas] level 1 function [`snrm2`][@stdlib/blas/base/snrm2].

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/array' );
var snrm2 = require( '@stdlib/blas/snrm2' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};

var x = array( discreteUniform( 10, 0, 100, opts ), {
    'shape': [ 5, 2 ]
});
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var y = snrm2( x, -1 );
console.log( ndarray2array( y ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
